title: A higher hydrogen level
hook: Change principal quantum number and predict binding-energy magnitude.
misconception: binding-energy magnitude doubles when principal quantum number doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply abs(E_n) = 13.6 eV/n² to compare binding-energy magnitude when principal quantum number changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With the nonrelativistic Bohr model of hydrogen with allowed positive integer levels, abs(E_n) = 13.6 eV/n². When principal quantum number doubles, binding-energy magnitude becomes ¼ times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model abs(E_n) = 13.6 eV/n²; scaling exponent -2. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider the nonrelativistic Bohr model of hydrogen with allowed positive integer levels, with a nonzero initial result. If principal quantum number triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on binding-energy magnitude?
recall.why: Apply abs(E_n) = 13.6 eV/n² under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/9.
